title: Why are U.S. highway exit numbers sometimes not consecutive?
sources: Federal Highway Administration Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices

lines.text: Have you ever noticed how highway exit numbers skip from Exit twelve straight to Exit twenty-five?
It is not because the department of transportation forgot how to count.
In the United States, most interstate highway exit numbers correspond directly to mile markers, not exit counts.
lines.caps: Exit numbers match *mile markers | not exit *counts!

lines.text: Exit twenty-five means you are exactly twenty-five miles away from the state border or highway beginning.
lines.caps: Exit 25 means you are *25 miles | from the state *line

lines.text: This mile-post system allows drivers to instantly calculate how many miles remain until their turn.
lines.caps: Drivers instantly calculate *miles | remaining to their *turn

lines.text: It also lets road engineers build brand new exits between existing ones without renumbering hundreds of signs.
lines.caps: New exits can be added *without | renumbering every *sign!

lines.text: The mile-marker system turns every highway into a giant built-in odometer for road trippers.
lines.caps: A built-in *ruler | spanning thousands of highway *miles!
